key_insight: The paper replaces ad hoc semi-local wall-scaling with elliptic equations that define a bounded density-corrected wall coordinate and transformed velocity fields before profile extraction.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more consistent inner-layer scaling for compressible wall turbulence with heat transfer, improving coordinate placement across boundary layers and channels.
method: Build a semi-local wall coordinate from local density and viscosity.
Solve a Helmholtz-type elliptic equation for a bounded density-induced correction to wall-normal stretching.
Use projection equations to obtain the transformed coordinate Y+ and projected velocity U+.
evidence_signal: A single set of wall-layer constants was calibrated on two cooled flat plates and then applied to zero-pressure-gradient boundary layers plus isothermal and mixed thermal-wall channels, with improved inner and buffer-layer placement reported.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate mean density, viscosity, wall distance, and wall-normal geometry, and the channel formulation relies on using the same wall-coordinate equation on half-domains with centerline-referenced density.
paper_title: Semi-local transformation for compressible wall turbulence via elliptic equations
